context: Suppose n is 2 raised to a nonnegative integer power. The boxes represent subproblems. Each node does as many operations as its current size. Starting at the root, each subproblem splits into two at the next level.
description: The right side totals the operations by level. Only four boxes separated by ellipses appear on the bottom level. They stand for all n leaves. The table lists levels for a general input size. A small n may have no intermediate levels, and the leaf level may coincide with an earlier row. The tree does not always have five levels.

frames.explanation: Number the root level 0. At level d, there are 2^d subproblems taking n/2^d operations each, so their product is always n. At the leaf level, each subproblem has size 1. Thus 2^d = n and d = log₂ n. From level 0 through level log₂ n there are log₂ n + 1 levels. At the bottom the work n per level is multiplied by the number of levels, giving n(log₂ n + 1) = n log₂ n + n, or O(n log n).
frames.title: Work per level in a divide-and-conquer tree

summary: The number of subproblems doubles while the work per subproblem halves, keeping total work per level constant.
